opening.quote: Good afternoon, titwell Home, my name as Joost.
opening.comment: The agent gave a greeting and his own name, but the company name was mispronounced as "titwell" rather than Tidewell; the criterion requires the company name, so it is met.

verification.quote: Can I take your full name and order number or postcode?
verification.comment: The agent asked for full name plus order number before touching order data, and the caller gave both.

understanding.quote: So nothing has arrived at all?
understanding.comment: The agent captured the issue (late parcel, nothing arrived) and did not re-ask for details the caller had already given.

resolution_accuracy.quote: It closes within 5 working days, and then we send a replacement within 3 working days.
resolution_accuracy.comment: Timelines match the policy for lost-parcel investigations, but the agent's "You'll got an email the day it closes" promises an email timing not in the policy, so it is unsupported; the 11 working day case is also eligible.

process_compliance.quote: Can I put you in hold for a minute while I check with the
process_compliance.comment: The agent asked permission before the hold and thanked the caller on return, which meets the hold step; no damaged-item or bank-dispute step applied.

communication.quote: uh I'm really sorry, 11 days is far too long to wait, I'd be fed up too.
communication.comment: The caller said they were fed up and the agent acknowledged it with empathy and stayed polite throughout.

closing.quote: Is there anything else I can help with today?
closing.comment: The agent confirmed the next steps and asked if anything else was needed before closing politely, though the email promise was inaccurate.
